description: G1: a visible lane and path network. Gates at every lot front, lanes joining them and the streets (a minimum spanning forest, kept off the lots), door paths out to the gates, a visible least width, every run on the relief.

sources.fixturesFrom: conformance/layout/ground-plan.json (copied byte for byte; the corpus test guards the copy)

cases.name: network: Brightwater Vale's settled village on its terrain
cases.note: Brightwater's seven lots after the settle (the layout corpus's followed plan), its two lanes and the square, the doors where the settle put them, on its terrain: every lot joins the streets (four by the square, two by the lanes, one through a neighbour's gate), every door gets a path to its gate, the seven old footpaths are superseded.

cases.name: network: Brightwater Vale's settled village on flat ground
cases.note: The same village with no terrain: the same lanes, every point at y 0 and every grade 0 — what the relief adds is the heights and the costs over the ground.

cases.name: reach: two gates 22.8 m apart are linked by a lane
cases.note: No street; two lots side by side whose gates stand 22.8 m apart (0.95 of the 24 m reach): one lane between them, both unjoined.

cases.name: reach: two gates 25.2 m apart are not linked
cases.note: The same at 25.2 m (1.05 of the reach): no lane.

cases.name: join: a street whose edge is 17.1 m from a lot's gate is joined
cases.note: One lot facing a road 17.1 m beyond its gate (0.95 of the 18 m street join): a lane to the road's centreline, the lot joined.

cases.name: join: a street whose edge is 18.9 m from a lot's gate is beyond reach
cases.note: The same road 18.9 m beyond the gate (1.05 of the join): no lane; the lot is unjoined and its door path still runs to its gate.

cases.name: clearance: a lot whose back is 1.535 m off the lane between two gates blocks it
cases.note: Lots a and c side by side, a small lot d in front of the gap between them with its back 1.535 m from the a–c lane's line: closer than a lane's half width and the clearance (1.25 + 0.3), so a and c are not linked directly.

cases.name: clearance: a lot whose back is 1.565 m off the lane between two gates lets it pass
cases.note: The same with d 1.565 m off: the lane between a and c is laid.

cases.name: visible: a stated 0.95 m lane and path are widened to 1 m
cases.note: A world stating a 0.95 m lane and a 0.95 m path (half 0.475, under the 0.5 m least half width): both drawn at half 0.5, noted lane-widened and path-widened.

cases.name: visible: a stated 1.05 m lane and path are drawn as stated
cases.note: The same at 1.05 m (half 0.525): drawn as stated, no note; the gate stands off by the stated half width.

cases.name: relief: a lane up a grade of 0.19 is walked
cases.note: A lot on ground rising 0.19 a metre towards its road (0.95 of the 0.2 walking grade): the lane and the door path climb it, not stepped.

cases.name: relief: a lane up a grade of 0.21 is stepped
cases.note: The same at 0.21 a metre (1.05 of the grade): the lane and the door path are stepped.

cases.name: relief: over a ridge, a back lot joins through its neighbour
cases.note: Lot b stands beside lot a facing it, 11.45 m from the road in plan and 15.45 m from a's gate along a's front; a 4 m ridge 5 m either side of z 55 lies between b and the road (x 60 on) but not under a's way: over the ground b's own way is the longer, so b joins through a's gate (and its direct way would have been stepped).

cases.name: relief: on flat ground, the same back lot joins the road itself
cases.note: The same two lots with no ridge: b joins the road directly, 13.45 m to its centreline against 15.45 m to a.

cases.name: unjoined: a lot behind another, facing its back, has no way through
cases.note: Lot b stands behind lot a facing a's back, the only street beyond a: b's lane would cross a, so b is unjoined (reported, not routed round).

cases.name: plaza: a gate on a plaza joins it where it stands
cases.note: A lot whose gate stands inside a plaza's outline: the join is a lane of no length at the gate, and the lot's old footpath strip is superseded by its door path.

cases.name: ties: two streets the same distance from a gate, the lower id is taken
cases.note: One lot between two roads 8 m either side of its gate's line: the gate joins the road whose id sorts first ('road.east' before 'road.west').

cases.name: doors: a door whose building has no lot, and no streets at all
cases.note: Two lots and no street: their gates are linked and both are unjoined; a door naming no lot in the plan is listed in noLot and gets no path.

cases.name: widths: a stated 0 m width takes the rules'
cases.note: A lane and path width of 0 (unstated): 1.25 and 0.6 m halves, no note.

cases.name: supersedes: a lot no door serves keeps its footpath
cases.note: Two lots on the square; a has a door and b none. G1 lays a's door path and supersedes a's footpath; b's footpath serves no door path and stays.

cases.name: doors: a door whose step-out point is its gate gets a path of one piece, no repeated end
cases.note: A door 0.55 m outside its lot's front, facing out: 1 m out of it is the gate (6.55 m from the lot's middle) itself, so the door path is the one piece from the door to the gate, with no repeated end vertex.

cases.name: doors: a back door's path goes round its own house the shorter way, then through the gate's gap
cases.note: A lot whose front (z = 5) faces a road, its house from z = 8 to 13, and a back door at (-1, 13) facing away from the road. Straight from its step-out point (-1, 14) to the gate the path would cross the house; it goes round the house's west corners pushed out by the step-out (1 m), the shorter way, and then, since the leg from (-4, 7) to the gate would cross the yard's front edge (0.3 m inside the front) 2.1 m off the gate's middle, outside the 3 m gap, it goes to the approach on the gate's axis a step-out inside that edge (0, 6.3) and out square through the gap (m2).

cases.name: doors: a corner side door's path keeps off its house's corner and enters the gate through the middle of its gap
cases.note: The same lot and house, with a side door at (3, 8.5) on the east wall by the front corner. Straight from its step-out point (4, 8.5) to the gate the path would pass 0.47 m from the house's corner, under its 0.6 m half width: it takes the corner pushed out (4, 7), and from there, as the leg to the gate would cross the front edge outside the gap, the approach (0, 6.3) and out square through the gap (m2).

cases.name: doors: with no outline stated, the same back door's path runs straight to the gate (the control)
cases.note: The back-door lot with its building's outline left out: the network cannot know the house is there, so the path runs straight from the step-out point (-1, 14) to the gate, as before m2; the gap rule alone does not apply, since the straight leg crosses the front edge 0.18 m off the gate's middle, inside the gap.

cases.name: doors: when the approach would stand on its own house, the path does not go through it
cases.note: The back-door lot with a house whose front comes to a point at (0, 6) on the gate's axis (a bay), and a side door at (3, 10) on its east wall. The path goes round the house's east corner (3, 8), pushed out, to (4, 7.46); from there the leg to the gate crosses the yard's front edge (z = 5.3) 1.84 m off the gate's middle, outside the gap. The approach on the gate's axis a step-out inside that edge would be (0, 6.3), 0.3 m from the bay's point, under the path's 0.6 m half width, so it is skipped: the path keeps its leg to the gate rather than run to a point on the house (m2).
